title: From the Chip Ban to the Power Grid
thesis: An export rule, a data-center groundbreaking, and a grid-shortfall warning filed to three different desks are one causal chain that no single agency owns end to end.
body:
Three stories filed under three different desks this month — trade, real estate, utilities — are the same story told in sequence [sy_1cfa44687550, sy_d4d66a02daef, sy_66ab57d60bca].

<connection layout="chain">
<node>An export rule caps advanced-GPU shipments, pushing demand toward domestic build-outs [sy_1cfa44687550].</node>
So the capital that cannot buy banned chips abroad pours into building at home —
<node>a hyperscaler breaks ground on a two-gigawatt campus, the largest single load ever proposed in the region [sy_d4d66a02daef].</node>
which lands, finally, on infrastructure that was never sized for it —
<node>the grid operator warns of summer shortfalls, naming data-center load as the swing factor [sy_66ab57d60bca].</node>
</connection>

<define term="interconnection queue">the waiting line a new power plant or large load joins before it is allowed to connect to the grid; today it can run for years</define>

The thread runs from a trade desk in Washington to a substation in the desert, and no single agency owns its whole length [sy_1cfa44687550, sy_66ab57d60bca].

<card kind="perspective">[pp_22254db1a21a]</card>
